methodological_rigor.justification: The study is a prespecified exploratory multiomic substudy nested in the CITN-12 phase 1 single-arm trial (NCT02595866) with longitudinal sampling at C01D01, C01D02, C01D08 and EOT. Strengths include multiple orthogonal readouts (bulk RNA-seq, scRNA-seq, plasma cytokines, flow cytometry, HIV DNA/RNA assays) and an in vitro HIV challenge in five healthy donors that mechanistically supports the IFN/TLR/HIV-restriction axis. Weaknesses: n=30 (only 14 to EOT, split 9 vs 5 for the central comparison), no randomization or control arm, 29/30 male precluding sex-stratified analyses, no formal power calculation (acknowledged), batch effects in bulk RNA-seq corrected with ComBat without diagnostics shown, and the ISGhi/ISGlo groups are defined post hoc from clustering on modules themselves associated with HIV DNA, creating circularity risk for group-stratified comparisons. Statistical choices are appropriate (Wilcoxon/Mann-Whitney, Spearman, GLM in edgeR with BH correction, GSEA permutations, LASSO with LOOCV, ridge regression) with effect sizes and nominal P values reported, though CIs are rarely given and multiplicity across many module-by-timepoint tests is only partially controlled.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The design is a prespecified exploratory immunologic substudy of a non-randomized open-label phase 1 trial, best classified as Oxford CEBM 2b (individual cohort / low-quality trial). Clinical relevance is substantial: PLWH with cancer are an underserved high-risk population, pembrolizumab is standard oncology care, and the identification of a baseline/early ISG signature predictive of HIV reservoir decline (median 2.39-fold reduction in HIV DNA in group 1) has direct translational implications for HIV cure strategies, patient selection and rationale for IFN/TLR-agonist or TGF-beta-inhibitor combinations. Endpoints include HIV DNA, inducible HIV RNA and plasma viremia (surrogate but field-standard reservoir measures) plus RECIST-like cancer response. The absence of IPDA, tissue sampling and an ART-interruption endpoint tempers immediate practice-change but the biomarker hypothesis is actionable in planned trials.

reporting_quality.justification: This is primarily a prognostic/predictive biomarker substudy of a trial cohort, so REMARK is the most applicable checklist (STROBE and ARRIVE partially apply to the human cohort and in vitro arm respectively). Reporting is thorough: trial registration (NCT02595866), prespecification of the exploratory substudy, participant flow and timepoint-specific sample availability (Supplementary Data 1 D3), detailed assay methods, antibody clones/catalog numbers, analytic pipelines and software versions. Weaker items: no CONSORT-style flow diagram, no formal risk-of-bias framing, limited reporting of adverse events in this manuscript (deferred to parent trial refs 27, 30), and multiplicity handling is only partially described. Data/code posture is good — a Zenodo deposit is cited (10.5281/zenodo.11200738) and the authors commit to GEO deposition of RNA-seq counts, though some data (uncorrected matrices) are described as pending.

novelty_literature.justification: The novelty is primarily empirical and conceptual: this is the most detailed longitudinal multiomic dissection to date of anti-PD-1 effects in PLWH with cancer, linking a preexisting myeloid/ISG state and a 24-hour TLR-ISG induction to durable HIV reservoir decline. Mapping the signature across ~1,000 public scRNA-seq datasets via SCimilarity to show generalizability of the ISG-high state is a methodological strength and a novel use of the atlas. Prior work in this space (Uldrick 2019/2022, SIV macaque PD-1 studies by Velu, Mylvaganam, Rahman; the DURVAST signature; Boukhaled Nat Immunol 2022 pre-encoded IFN signature) establishes the broader paradigm, so the paper extends rather than invents the concept, but the human in vivo PLWH-with-cancer context, the TGF-beta/IFN antagonism in vivo, and the in vitro HIV-restriction mechanistic loop fill a documented gap.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized, with a clear logical arc from systemic 24-hour effects to EOT stratification to subset-specific mechanisms to in vitro validation and a predictive model. The abstract is quantitatively grounded (29M/1F, 1 CR / 4 PR, 9/14 responders) and accurately reflects the paper, though one phrase ("across subsets of across subsets") is a copy-editing error. Figure legends are detailed and standalone-interpretable, statistical tests are explicitly named per panel, and acronyms are generally expanded on first use. Minor issues: methods section repeats cohort description verbatim across subsections, some paragraphs in Results are dense with module numbering that is hard to track without the figures, and the Discussion occasionally drifts into mechanistic speculation (trained immunity, epigenetic reprogramming) that is not directly tested.

key_strengths: Rich prespecified longitudinal multiomic design (bulk + scRNA-seq + cytokines + flow + HIV virology) in a rare and clinically important cohort of PLWH with advanced cancer on pembrolizumab (NCT02595866)

Convergent evidence across platforms: baseline and 24-hour induction of myeloid/ISG/TLR modules predicts HIV DNA decline at EOT (median 2.39-fold reduction in group 1), with 8/9 group-1 participants showing reduced inducible HIV RNA
Mechanistic in vitro validation showing type I/II IFN and TLR3/7/8 agonists restrict HIV infection via APOBEC3G/IFIT1 induction, with abrogation by IFN-receptor blockade
SCimilarity mapping to ~1000 public scRNA-seq datasets provides unusually strong external generalizability evidence for the ISG-high state
Transparent methods, Zenodo code deposit (10.5281/zenodo.11200738) and planned GEO submission, detailed antibody and software reporting
key_concerns: Small sample size (n=30 enrolled, n=14 to EOT, 9 vs 5 for the central ISGhi/ISGlo comparison) with no randomization or control arm and no formal power calculation
ISGhi/ISGlo groups are defined post hoc from clustering on modules themselves associated with HIV DNA, introducing circularity in group-stratified reservoir analyses
Severe sex imbalance (29 males, 1 female) precluding any sex-stratified analysis of a therapy with known sex-dependent immunologic effects
Lack of IPDA (intact proviral) measurement and absence of tissue sampling limits confidence that peripheral HIV DNA changes reflect replication-competent reservoir decay
Multiplicity correction is applied within some analyses (BH in edgeR) but not systematically across the large number of module-by-timepoint-by-group comparisons; confidence intervals rarely reported
Minor copy-editing issues in the abstract (e.g., "across subsets of across subsets")
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically rigorous, mechanistically rich human multiomic study in a hard-to-recruit population with convergent in vivo signatures and in vitro causal validation; translational implications for HIV cure strategies and ICB patient selection justify a top-tier venue, pending clarifications on post-hoc group definition and multiplicity.
